item.title: ‘The Weight’ Review: Ethan Hawke Elevates A Rugged, Predictable Gold-Run Survivalist Western[Sundance]
item.description: As far as one can tell, Murphy (Ethan Hawke), a father, WWI veteran, and avid car mechanic, has never encountered an insurmountable challenge. Living in Eugene, Oregon, in 1933, four years into the Great Depression, Murphy and his young daughter, Penny (the adorable Avy Berry), are evicted from their home. To no fault of his own, the search for a new place is the inciting incident in “The Weight,” the feature debut from director Padraic McKinley. Continue reading ‘The Weight’ Review: Ethan Hawke

item.title: ‘Tell Me Everything’ Review: A Tale Of Complex Father-Son Betrayal That Doesn’t Say Enough [Sundance]
item.description: Moshe Rosenthal’s second feature, “Tell Me Everything,” billed by Sundance as a drama about a boy reckoning with a “shattering truth” about his father (Assi Cohen) at the height of the AIDS crisis, straddles two timelines. There’s the protagonist, Boaz, at age 12 in 1987 (played by the talented young newcomer Yair Mazor), and then there’s Boaz in 1996 (played by Ido Tako). item.title: ‘Aanikoobijigan’ Review: Adam & Zack Khalil Craft A Quietly Radical Documentary About Life, Death, Time, & Knowledge [Sundance]
item.description: “Aanikoobijigan [ancestor/great-grandparent/great-grandchild],” the thoughtful and quietly radical new documentary from Ojibwe filmmakers Adam and Zack Khalil, which recently won the NEXT Audience Award at Sundance, is about a great many things. It’s about life just as it is death, theft as much as it is restoration, and history just as much as it is our current moment. item.title: HBO’s Casey Bloys Won’t Fully Close ‘Euphoria’ Books & Leaves It Up To Creator Sam Levinson’s Decision
item.description: For a show the internet has spent the better part of two years treating like a closed chapter, “Euphoria” remains, at least from HBO’s perspective, aggressively unresolved. And if anyone was hoping for a neat “final season” declaration ahead of Season 3, Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO, HBO and Max Content, is making it clear that’s not where the network’s head is—because the decision, as he frames it, isn’t really HBO’s to make yet.
